bridge.note: Both thank the same goddess by different names: Italian says fortuna where everyday Spanish says suerte — and each language HAS the other's noun, at a dressier register. A vocabulary flip wearing a preposition costume.

interference.es_to_it: 'Per sorte' is not the Italian marker — fortune does the job: per fortuna.
interference.it_to_es: 'Por fortuna' exists and is fine, slightly bookish; everyday Spanish runs on luck: por suerte.
